clue.text: Incas ate production of ranch

indicators.note: a production of something is a fresh staging of it, so these letters are put on in a new order

explanation.surface: Incas ate the output of a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' rearranges the eight letters of INCAS ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An estancia is a large cattle estate in South America, a kind of ranch.

clue.text: Opponents notice officer

parts.note: East and North are opposing seats at the bridge table, so E and N
a notice is a sign put up for people to read

explanation.surface: An officer notices his adversaries.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge North-South play against East-West, so any E and N pair are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a junior commissioned rank, historically the lowest infantry officer who carried the flag.

clue.text: Being embraced by creature with warts, old boy? Tough!

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so the old boy sits within the creature

parts.note: a toad is the amphibian famous for warty skin
OB is the standard abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil hugged by a warty animal is told to put up with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive exclamations meaning that nothing can be done and the listener must accept it.

clue.text: Over time, sunshine breaks into shelter

indicators.note: over here means in addition, so the time letter is tacked on at the end
the word is broken into pieces and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: After a while the sun bursts into a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' here means on top of that, so the time letter comes last rather than being mixed into the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nissen hut is a prefabricated semicircular corrugated-iron building used as a wartime shelter.

clue.text: Fact-finding body in full flow about Trojan 'ero

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the flowing phrase wraps round the hero

parts.note: a river in spate is in full flood, so in full flow gives IN SPATE
Hector was the great Trojan hero; the dropped aitch of 'ero tells us to drop his H too

explanation.surface: An investigative team pours out its account of a Cockney-spoken Trojan champion.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ero shows a dropped H, so Hector becomes ECTOR, which goes inside IN SPATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspectorate is an official body of inspectors charged with examining and reporting facts.

clue.text: Good scope for manoeuvre

parts.note: ambit means extent or scope

explanation.surface: A promising amount of room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is an opening move or ploy calculated to gain an advantage, a type of manoeuvre.

clue.text: A friend in Miami gossips

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pal in a Florida city who talks about people behind their backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for friend, used informally in English for a pal.

clue.text: Collect old coin in handkerchief

parts.note: to band together is to gather or collect
the anna was a former coin of India, a sixteenth of a rupee

explanation.surface: Gathering a historic coin wrapped in a hanky.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandanna is a large coloured handkerchief, often tied round the head or neck.

clue.text: Trustee's ill-disposed and cross

parts.note: averse means opposed or unwilling, ill-disposed towards something

explanation.surface: A trustee is in a bad mood and angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Trustee's is read as 'is', a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to travel across, so it can stand for the verb cross.

clue.text: Film director makes a hit about southern Spain

indicators.note: about means going round, so the hit encloses the southern Spanish letters

parts.note: a score is a hit or success, as in scoring a goal
ES is the international code for Spain, as in the .es web domain

explanation.surface: A movie maker achieves success in Andalusia.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American filmmaker behind Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

clue.text: Insane preparation of pigment

indicators.note: preparing something means making it up from its ingredients, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A mad way of mixing paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preparation of' rearranges the letters of INSANE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, raw or burnt, used by painters for yellow-brown and red-brown shades.

clue.text: I'm a model, else (amazingly) I give French lessons

indicators.note: amazingly suggests something astonishing has happened to the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A model reveals that she is, surprisingly, also a French teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazingly' rearranges the twelve letters of I'M A MODEL ELSE.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the French teacher, if a young woman, was traditionally addressed by the French honorific for an unmarried lady.

clue.text: Greek champion's charm

parts.note: an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: The appeal of a Greek sporting hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Grace and charm are synonyms for an attractive elegance of manner.

clue.text: Detailed discourse follows return of package

indicators.note: follows places the discourse word after the turned package
returning the package means turning its letters back to front

parts.note: a bale is a bundled package of goods such as hay or cotton
to orate is to discourse or speak at length

explanation.surface: A thorough talk comes after a parcel is sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: A package of hay or cotton is a classic crossword sense of the word; 'Detailed' is an adjective, matching the answer used as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate as an adjective means intricate and full of detail.

clue.text: Holds tightly when restraining pugilist? That shows guts!

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so the boxer is kept inside the clinging word

parts.note: to cling is to grip something firmly
a pugilist is a boxer, a hitter

explanation.surface: Gripping a boxer while he is held back demonstrates courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' looks like courage in the surface, but it is the literal sense: intestines.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitterlings are the small intestines of a pig, cooked as food, so literally guts.

clue.text: Help finish a hotel in the country

indicators.note: in puts the finish, a and hotel inside the country word

parts.note: land can mean a country or nation
end means finish
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Assistance with closing down a rural guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To lend a hand is the idiom for giving help.

clue.text: Stress keeping identification in disaster

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so the stress word contains the identification

parts.note: accent is stress or emphasis on a syllable

explanation.surface: The strain of carrying papers in a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unfortunate mishap, a minor or major disaster.

clue.text: Evangelist with detachment is halfhearted

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers called Evangelists
an arm is a branch or detachment of the armed forces

explanation.surface: A gospel writer who keeps his distance lacks enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm figuratively means tepid in feeling, lacking enthusiasm.

clue.text: Consider 'er intention in arrangement

parts.note: to count something as true is to consider it so
the clue already gives the word with its aitch dropped, so take it as written
the point of something is its purpose or intention

explanation.surface: Weigh up what she means in a planned layout.
explanation.definitionFit: Counterpoint is a musical arrangement combining independent melodic lines.

clue.text: Turner accepts love and hate

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the turner holds the love letter

parts.note: a lathe is a machine that turns wood or metal
love is nil in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A painter named Turner welcomes love and loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner looks like the painter J.M.W. Turner, but it is a machine that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest, a strong synonym for hate.

clue.text: Cambridge college has tons of wine

parts.note: Clare is one of the colleges of Cambridge University
T is the abbreviation for ton or tons

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college keeps a large stock of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Supporters at the rink find Ray tucking into desserts

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the fish is placed within the desserts

parts.note: ices are frozen desserts
a skate is a kind of ray, the flat fish

explanation.surface: Fans at an ice arena see Ray eating pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating, but here it means going inside. Ray looks like a name; it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice skates are what support a skater on the ice, punningly cast as supporters at the rink.

clue.text: They say little Helen is sound

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is spoken, its sound giving the answer

parts.note: Nell is a pet form of the name Helen

explanation.surface: People report that small Helen is in good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy, but it is the noun for a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A knell is the sound of a bell tolled, especially at a death.

clue.text: Island in the form of a ring

parts.note: to toll a bell is to ring it

explanation.surface: A description of a coral island shaped like a hoop.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description, but 'a ring' is wordplay: ring as a verb, as a bell is rung.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped coral reef or island enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: The Castilian retains reputation for fast finish

indicators.note: retains means keeps hold of inside, so the Spanish article holds the reputation

parts.note: el is the Spanish (Castilian) word for the
a name is a reputation, as in making a name for yourself

explanation.surface: A Spaniard keeps his good name for a quick ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast finish' looks like a race's end; fast here means durable.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard, durable glossy coating, a finish that stays fast.

clue.text: Leo tears out a shrub

indicators.note: out suggests things put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Leo rips out a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of LEO TEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleaster is a Mediterranean shrub, also called Russian olive or wild olive.

clue.text: Upheaval of stomach in the previous month

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach
ult, short for ultimo, is the formal letter-writing term for last month

explanation.surface: Stomach trouble from last month.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumult is a disorderly commotion, a state of upheaval.

clue.text: A draw is boring — hard to swallow

parts.note: dead can mean dull or lifeless, so boring
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
to eat is to swallow food

explanation.surface: A tie is dull and difficult to accept.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race or contest ending in a tie, a draw.
